pages.title: Electronics
pages.description: Electronics tools on stevenphilley.com — watts to amps, amps to watts, and Ohm's law. Runs in the browser.

pages.title: 555 timer — Electronics
pages.description: NE555 astable and monostable timing from R and C. Live frequency, period, duty cycle, and pulse width.

pages.title: Capacitor codes — Electronics
pages.description: Interactive EIA capacitor marking decoder. Read a 3-digit code to pF / nF / µF, or look up a value and snap to a nearby E12 code.

pages.title: Circuit explorer — Electronics
pages.description: Beginner interactive circuit explorer and trainer. Loops, Ohm's law, series, parallel, LEDs, capacitors, RC time, voltage dividers, Kirchhoff, Thévenin, Norton, Superposition, diode I-V, mesh/nodal equations, BJT common-emitter bias, and FET/MOSFET voltage-controlled switching.

pages.title: Current divider — Electronics
pages.description: Two parallel resistors split a source current. Set Iin, R1, and R2; get branch currents, voltage, and power.

pages.title: dB / dBm — Electronics
pages.description: Live dB and dBm converter: power ratio, voltage ratio, dBm ↔ mW, and dBW ↔ W.

pages.title: Impedance — Electronics
pages.description: Series or parallel RLC impedance: |Z| and phase from f, R, L, and C. Xl = 2πfL, Xc = 1/(2πfC).

pages.title: Inductor codes — Electronics
pages.description: Interactive EIA/IEC inductor color code decoder. Click the bands to read µH / mH / H and tolerance, or type a value and snap to a nearby E12 hobbyist code.

pages.title: LED resistor — Electronics
pages.description: Pick supply volts, LED forward voltage, and desired milliamps. Get the series resistor, nearest E24 value, and power in the resistor.

pages.title: Op-amp gain — Electronics
pages.description: Inverting, non-inverting, and ideal differential op-amp gain from Rf and Rin (or Rg). Live Av in V/V and dB, optional Vin → Vout.

pages.title: Peak detector — Electronics
pages.description: Simple diode peak detector and ideal precision rectifier. Set Vin peak, Vf, C, Rload, and f; get held peak, ripple, and discharge notes live.

pages.title: Q-factor — Electronics
pages.description: Series or parallel RLC Q-factor and bandwidth: f₀, Z₀, Q, BW, and −3 dB band edges from R, L, and C.

pages.title: RC filter — Electronics
pages.description: First-order RC low-pass and high-pass filter calculator. fc = 1/(2πRC), plus gain and phase at a chosen frequency.

pages.title: RC time — Electronics
pages.description: RC time constant from R and C. τ = R × C, plus 1τ / 3τ / 5τ charge and discharge times.

pages.title: Reactance — Electronics
pages.description: AC reactance from frequency and C or L. Xc = 1/(2πfC), Xl = 2πfL, plus |Z| and phase with series R.

pages.title: Rectifier — Electronics
pages.description: Half-wave, full-wave, and bridge rectifier helper. Set Vin peak, Vf, C, Rload, and f; get Vout peak, ripple frequency, and ΔV ≈ I/(fr C) live.

pages.title: Resistor codes — Electronics
pages.description: Interactive resistor color code decoder. Click the bands to read ohms and tolerance, or type a value and get a nearest 4-band code.

pages.title: LC resonance — Electronics
pages.description: LC resonance from L and C. f0 = 1/(2π√(LC)), ω0, characteristic Z0, plus series Q and bandwidth when R is set.

pages.title: RL filter — Electronics
pages.description: First-order RL low-pass and high-pass filter calculator. fc = R/(2πL), plus gain and phase at a chosen frequency.

pages.title: RL time — Electronics
pages.description: RL time constant from R and L. τ = L / R, plus 1τ / 3τ / 5τ current marks and a rough corner scale.

pages.title: Schmitt trigger / comparator — Electronics
pages.description: Ideal comparator and Schmitt trigger. Set Vin, Vref, rails, and R1/R2; get thresholds, hysteresis, and HIGH/LOW state live.

pages.title: Series & parallel — Electronics
pages.description: Combine resistors in series or parallel. Set two to four ohms; get Req and the nearest E24 value.

pages.title: Turns ratio — Electronics
pages.description: Ideal transformer turns-ratio helper: Vp, Np, Ns → Vs (and Is). Mutual inductance M = k√(L1 L2) from two inductors and coupling.

pages.title: Voltage divider — Electronics
pages.description: Two resistors split a supply. Set Vin, R1, and R2; get Vout, current, and power in each resistor.

pages.title: Wheatstone bridge — Electronics
pages.description: Four-resistor Wheatstone bridge. Set Vin and the arms; get Va, Vb, Vg, and balance. Solve R4 when balanced.

pages.title: Z80 — Electronics
pages.description: Zilog Z80 information hub — history, John Winans Z80 Retro!, Zeal 8-bit Computer, CP/M, homebrew SBCs, tools, and a curated link directory.

pages.title: Zener regulator — Electronics
pages.description: Shunt zener regulator helper. Set Vin, Vz, Rs, and Rload; get Vout, Iz, load current, and power in the diode and series resistor live.

pages.title: Astronomy — Solar map · Moon · tides · local sky · stars · exoplanets · galaxy
pages.description: Astronomy desk: solar system map with day and time controls, Moon phases, Venus phases (inner orbit), planet phases (Mercury through Neptune, including Jupiter from a spacecraft), eclipses (why not every month), tides (spring and neap), local sky, seasons (axial tilt), retrograde (Earth overtaking Mars), opposition…

pages.title: Eclipses — why not every month
pages.description: Interactive Earth–Moon–Sun eclipse desk. The Moon’s orbit is tilted about 5°, so most new and full Moons miss. Slide the node offset to see an umbra and penumbra, or a shadow that misses. Educational schematic, not a prediction.

pages.title: Exoplanets — discovery methods & notable worlds
pages.description: Educational exoplanet desk: how we find planets around other stars (transit, radial velocity, imaging, microlensing, timing) and a curated teaching set of 100+ confirmed worlds from NASA public records — not a catalog dump.

pages.title: Galaxy start — Milky Way orientation — Steven PhilleyMilky Way spiral arms schematic
pages.description: Beginner Milky Way orientation: spiral arms overview, Sol’s approximate seat in the Orion Arm, a CSS/SVG scale diagram, and a short galactic glossary. Educational start — not a Gaia dump.

pages.title: Jupiter — full from Earth, crescent from a spacecraft
pages.description: Interactive Jupiter phases: from Earth the disk stays about 99% lit or more, a maximum phase angle of arcsin(1/5.204) from the NASA fact sheet. Drag a spacecraft observer to see the crescent Voyager, Cassini, and Juno recorded.

pages.title: Local sky — city or ZIP
pages.description: Approximate sky orientation by city or ZIP. Defaults to Campbell, CA (95008). Seasonal constellations and major landmarks with month and local-time controls. Client-side sidereal math — no paid APIs.

pages.title: Mars — gibbous to full, never a crescent
pages.description: Interactive Mars phases desk: a superior planet. From Earth the disk stays gibbous to full. The maximum phase angle is arcsin of 1 over the NASA fact-sheet orbit ratio 1.524. Classroom circles, not an ephemeris.

pages.title: Mercury — phases of the innermost orbit
pages.description: Interactive Mercury phases desk: an orbit inside Earth’s, so we see crescent through gibbous. Inferior and superior conjunction, and the evening and morning elongations. Classroom circles, not an ephemeris.

pages.title: Moon — phases & observing
pages.description: Moon phase for any date and time: dial, illumination, age, and phase name, with a Now button for your local clock. Educational schematic, cited to Meeus and NASA.

pages.title: Nearest stars — Sol’s neighborhood
pages.description: Interactive list and distance-scale of the nearest stars to Sol: Proxima Centauri, Alpha Centauri, Barnard’s Star, Wolf 359, and more — distances in light-years and spectral types.

pages.title: Neptune — nearly full from Earth
pages.description: Interactive Neptune phases: a superior planet. From Earth the disk stays gibbous to full. Maximum phase angle arcsin(1/30.178) from the NASA fact sheet, minimum lit fraction 99.97%. Classroom circles, not an ephemeris.

pages.title: Opposition — an outer planet opposite the Sun
pages.description: Interactive opposition desk: Earth between the Sun and Mars, so an outer planet stands opposite the Sun. Conjunction hides it near the Sun. Quadrature is the right angle. Classroom circles, not an ephemeris.

pages.title: Planet phases — crescent, gibbous, and what Earth can see
pages.description: Planet phases: Mercury and Venus run crescent to full. Mars through Neptune stay gibbous to full from Earth. Minimum lit fractions are computed from NASA fact-sheet orbit ratios. Jupiter adds a spacecraft view.

pages.title: Retrograde — Earth laps Mars
pages.description: Interactive retrograde desk: Earth on a faster inner orbit catches Mars. The line of sight swings backward for a stretch. The orbit does not reverse. Classroom circles, not an ephemeris.

pages.title: Saturn — nearly full from Earth
pages.description: Interactive Saturn phases: a superior planet. From Earth the disk stays gibbous to full. Maximum phase angle arcsin(1/9.573) from the NASA fact sheet, minimum lit fraction 99.73%. Classroom circles, not an ephemeris.

pages.title: Seasons — axial tilt, not distance
pages.description: Interactive Earth seasons desk: axial tilt of about 23.4° stays parallel around the Sun. Walk the year, compare hemispheres, and read approximate day length by latitude — nearly 12 hours everywhere near equinox.

pages.title: Stars — types, color, and life phases
pages.description: Interactive color lesson on stellar spectral types OBAFGKM and life phases: protostar, main sequence, red giant, planetary nebula, white dwarf, supernova, neutron star, black hole. Educational schematic — not a research tool.

pages.title: Tides — two bulges, spring and neap
pages.description: Interactive tides desk: the Moon’s gravity raises two ocean bulges, Earth turns under them, and the Sun adds or partly cancels. Spring at new and full; neap at the quarters. Classroom schematic, not a tide table.

pages.title: Uranus — nearly full from Earth
pages.description: Interactive Uranus phases: a superior planet. From Earth the disk stays gibbous to full. Maximum phase angle arcsin(1/19.165) from the NASA fact sheet, minimum lit fraction 99.93%. Classroom circles, not an ephemeris.

pages.title: Venus — phases of an inner orbit
pages.description: Interactive Venus phases desk: an orbit inside Earth’s, so we see crescent through gibbous. Inferior and superior conjunction, and the evening and morning elongations. Classroom circles, not an ephemeris.

pages.title: Atmosphere — layers & heights — Steven PhilleyEarth atmosphere layers cross-section
pages.description: Interactive cross-section of Earth’s atmosphere: troposphere through exosphere — approximate heights, temperature trends, and what each layer needs environmentally.

pages.title: The ice crop — mining frozen water
pages.description: History of ice harvesting from Mari and the Zhou ice pits through the frozen-water trade to lunar prospecting. Commercial ice came from lakes, rivers, and mountain glaciers. Polar bulk shipping did not happen. Cited.

pages.title: Electromagnetic spectrum — radio to gamma
pages.description: Interactive electromagnetic-spectrum literacy: tap Radio through Gamma, then slide a Wien’s-law peak across a schematic. Cited NASA classroom ranges. Educational cartoon — not a lab instrument or medical advice.

pages.title: 3D graphics literacy — frames, pivots, handedness
pages.description: Interactive 3D graphics literacy: coordinate frames, vectors vs points, TRS order, camera look-at, winding; fulcrum/pivot rotation (local vs world); left vs right handedness with a flipable axis gizmo. API tendencies (OpenGL/Vulkan vs DirectX) with citations and disclaimers. Educational schematic — not a GPU course.

pages.title: Gravity — weight, orbits, spacetime
pages.description: Interactive gravity literacy: everyday weight and free fall, Newton’s inverse-square law, Einstein’s spacetime curvature, why the Standard Model omits gravity, and honest cosmology hooks. Cited NASA / NIST / CERN. Educational schematic — not a GR course.

pages.title: Letting the planet light the way — light pollution — Steven PhilleyUnshielded uplight vs full-cutoff shielding
pages.description: Educational desk on light pollution: skyglow, glare, and trespass; wildlife and human circadian/sleep literacy with reputable cites; practical DarkSky fixes (shields, ≤3000K, timers); Bay Area night-sky angle. Not medical advice.

pages.title: Day for Night — Salesforce Tower, skyglow, and a South Bay glance
pages.description: Educational essay on Jim Campbell’s Day for Night on Salesforce Tower: inward-facing LEDs, civic diary, skyglow literacy, and South Bay / Peninsula unease. Cited public sources. Not medical or legal advice.

pages.title: Ore mining & lithium — interactive lesson
pages.description: Interactive science literacy on ore mining and lithium: grade/tonnage toy, brine vs hard-rock vs clay paths, processing stages, geography, and environmental/social notes. Cross-links the material rushes history lesson.

pages.title: Ocean metals — iron fertilization vs mining particles
pages.description: Educational desk separating ocean iron fertilization (LOHAFEX, EIFEX: sinking algae, not documented mass fish kills) from deep-sea mining metal-particle experiments with documented coral, copepod, and fish-model harm. Cited sources. Not cheerleading geoengineering or mining.

pages.title: Humanoid robots, 2025–2026 — from parkour to early shifts
pages.description: Status essay on humanoid robots in 2025–2026: learned whole-body policies, early factory and logistics pilots, and first volume claims. Cited public sources. Company claims and supply-chain reports can outrun verified deployments. Not investment or safety advice.

pages.title: Standard Model — quarks, leptons, bosons
pages.description: Interactive Standard Model literacy: six quarks, six leptons, gauge bosons, the Higgs, three generations, and three forces. Gravity, dark matter, and neutrino mass sit outside or at the edge. Educational schematic — not a QFT course.

pages.title: Computer history timeline — Science
pages.description: Interactive timeline of computing, from the abacus and the Antikythera mechanism through ENIAC, the Z80, Unix, the Web, and modern AI. Pan, zoom, filter, and open sourced milestones.

pages.title: Northern vs Southern Hemisphere waves
pages.description: Why Northern and Southern Hemisphere ocean waves differ — fetch, land–ocean layout, Southern Ocean storm belt, Arctic ice loss — and what observations and IPCC-linked studies say is changing.
